newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts dismiss Roche purchase theory.
newsitem.headline: Analysts dismiss Roche purchase theory.

text.p: Analysts contacted by Reuters were overwhelingly sceptical about market rumours that Swiss drugs giant Roche might buy Sweden's Astra. Following is a selection of analysts' comments.

JOHN REEVES, PARIBAS - "This is such a huge amount that it has to be very doubtful. Astra and SmithKline have about the same market cap, around $30 billion. The biggest corporate purchase Roche has been involved in up to now has been when they bought Syntex for $5.3 billion. Astra or SmithKline would cost at least eight times as much."

NIGEL BARNES, MERRILL LYNCH - "It's not like the Swiss to make such aggressive bids. It's not really their style. I think some people have been a bit too hasty. The sector is heading towards more consolidation and this is definitely the type of rumour to get the market excited. Many feel Roche had their nose put out of joint when Ciba Geigy and Sandoz merged into Novartis and that Roche are now after something. What's more Roche have said they are not interested in a major purchase."
IAN SMITH, LEHMAN BROTHERS - "It's even less likely than Roche buying up Zeneca."
